gogpt_captive_prior: Both listed neighbors (Tiger III power station / gogpt_plant_id 100000408825, and Vlora Floating Thermal Power Plant / gogpt_plant_id 100000408826) are the same asset class: KESH's leased 'Tiger 1' and 'Tiger 3' floating thermal power ships (110 MW combined), operated by Renco and 100%-owned by Excelerate Energy LP. Per Balkan Green Energy News, these are HEAVY FUEL OIL-fired internal-combustion power barges leased to Albania's utility KESH since 2022 -- not gas-fired, and not part of the Port of Vlora FSRU 2 project (different owner chain: Excelerate/Renco vs. the terminal's current owner Aktor LNG USA). These are also the 'unfunctional oil-fired power plant' the new Aktor/Atlantic SEE LNG Trade MOU proposes to convert to gas in the future -- a proposed future PowerPlantsSupplied relationship, not a present one, and not captive to the terminal either way. Independent source: https://balkangreenenergynews.com/us-italian-consortium-to-lease-oil-fired-power-plant-to-albania/
confirmed_how: VERDICT: INSUFFICIENT. No FSRU vessel is currently named for this project and no design/engineering document describing onboard or on-site generation has been published. The project is at MOU/feasibility stage (Aktor LNG USA / Atlantic SEE LNG Trade deal with Albania's Albgaz, signed and updated April-June 2026, gas deliveries not targeted to start until 2030); the original 2021 Excelerate/ExxonMobil FSRU proposal (vessel Excelsior) was shelved after the vessel was reassigned to Germany in Oct 2022, with no replacement vessel ever announced. EVIDENCE: PR Newswire (Mar 12, 2021): Excelerate Energy, ExxonMobil LNG Market Development, and Albania's Ministry of Infrastructure and Energy signed an MOU 'to conduct a feasibility study for the potential development of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) Project in the Port of Vlora' -- no vessel or equipment named at this stage. Balkan Green Energy News (published Apr 29, 2026, updated Jun 2, 2026), 'Aktor LNG USA signs 20-year supply deal with Albania's Albgaz': Aktor LNG USA (a subsidiary of Greece's Aktor Group) and state-owned Albgaz signed a 20-year, USD 6 billion gas supply agreement, deliveries starting 2030; this follows an earlier 2026 memorandum between Albania and Atlantic SEE LNG Trade (JV of Aktor Group 60% + DEPA Commercial) 'envisag[ing] conducting studies on the development, construction and operation of a complex in Albania including a 380 MW natural gas-fired power plant' at Vlora, 'where an unfunctional oil-fired power plant would be converted to gas,' plus 'an LNG terminal... built at the port' and a pipeline to TAP via Fier. Neither source names an FSRU vessel, describes terminal-side power equipment, or gives any spec for on-site/onboard generation at the LNG terminal itself -- the whole complex is still at the MOU/study phase. Absence of a published design is treated as INSUFFICIENT, not NO, per the terminal-specific instruction that a documented vessel or design doc is required before ruling this out.
